params.why: keeps the volume well clear of a rounding boundary at 1 decimal place, so every correct use of the calculator's pi key rounds the same way

stem: The volume of a cylinder is the area of its circular base multiplied by its height. A cylinder has a radius of ${=r}$ cm and a height of ${=h}$ cm. Calculate the volume of the cylinder in $\text{cm}^3$, correct to 1 decimal place. Use the $\pi$ button on your calculator.
solution: Find the area of the circular base: $\text{area of base} = \pi r^{2} = \pi({=r})^{2} = {=r * r}\pi \text{ cm}^{2}$
Multiply the area of the base by the height of the cylinder: $V = \text{area of base} \times \text{height} = {=r * r}\pi \times {=h} = {=r * r * h}\pi \text{ cm}^{3}$
Use the $\pi$ button on your calculator and round to 1 decimal place: $V = {=r * r * h}\pi \approx {=fixed(pi * r ** 2 * h, 1)} \text{ cm}^{3}$
Write the final answer: the volume of the cylinder is ${=fixed(pi * r ** 2 * h, 1)}$ $\text{cm}^{3}$.
notes: Entry point of the skill, modelled on book worked example 7 (r = 4 cm, h = 15 cm, 1 d.p.; figure seen, radius labelled, height labelled). The figure cannot be sampled, so the stem gives both measurements in words. The stem states the book's own definition (area of base x height) as a scaffold; the solution follows the book's two steps exactly (base area, then multiply by the height). r is 2 to 6 and h is 3 to 12 (never equal to r), so volumes run from about 38 to 1357 cm^3 (40 clean instances). A require keeps the volume at least 0.1 of a unit in the first decimal place away from a rounding tie, so a solver using the calculator's pi (or 3.14159) gets the same rounded answer. The stem tells the student to use the pi button; an answer worked with 3.14 is not intended to be accepted. Numeric answer is unitless (cm^3 is stated in the stem). No mcq: the misconception list for this objective is empty.
